advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the rubric-body prose-marker grep in test_rubric_states_every_gate_and_check with a structural assertion (e.g. that the criterion loads and its rendered descriptor carries the S1-S3/(a)-(d) contract) or drop it in favor of the 36ab behavior fixtures.
evidence: `assert marker in RUBRIC.read_text(), f"rubric is missing {marker!r}"` (test_t15_overlay_derisk_criterion.py:43)

RUBRIC_REQUIRED = ("S1", "S2", "S3", "RISK NAMED", "FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF", "PROVE-THEN-CODIFY", "SCOPED CLEANUP", "ANTI-FP") — all are prose headings in the rubric body (plan_review_T15.md:12-23), read by the LLM finder, not by any non-human parser
Rule-5 litmus: an LLM is NOT a non-human consumer, so a prose/heading grep that merely guards the author's wording is a change-detector, not a structural-boundary assertion
advisory.finding: test_rubric_states_every_gate_and_check asserts that literal prose tokens ('RISK NAMED', 'FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF', 'PROVE-THEN-CODIFY', 'SCOPED CLEANUP', 'ANTI-FP', 'S1'..'S3') appear verbatim in the rubric .md body. These markers are prose consumed only by the LLM reviewer — no parser/validator/registry branches on the exact strings — so this is a wording-guard change-detector, not a structural-contract assertion. A behavior-preserving reword of the rubric would break the test with no change to observable T15 behaviour.
